discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: strongly correlated electrons and moiré quantum materials
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that at a 'magic' twist angle near 1.1 degrees the Dirac bands of bilayer graphene become nearly flat, so that interactions dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group confirmed this, finding correlated insulating states and, on doping, superconductivity with a phase diagram strikingly similar to that of the cuprates. The work created the field of twistronics and moiré quantum matter. For the first time, a strongly correlated electron system has a band filling, bandwidth and displacement field that can be tuned in situ with a gate. It has since produced orbital ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, nematicity and intertwined orders, and fractional Chern insulators in related moiré systems. This platform has changed how our whole community approaches high-temperature superconductivity and correlated electrons. After more than a decade of reproduction and extension, the contribution is broad, deep and durable.
